run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: No evidence for the cluster the question names exists in any source I could read: every document in `app-264-prod-logs` carries `cluster=staging-eu-west-2` and `environment=staging`, so nothing from that index can be named as the cause of checkout 500s in production-eu-west-2. The index holds only 3 documents in the authorized window (2026-11-20T06:15:33Z–2026-11-21T06:15:33Z), all staging-labelled: two `checkout-service` ERROR lines and one `payment-service` WARN line. For staging-eu-west-2 those lines report (a) at 04:15:24Z "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress" and (b) at 05:15:24Z "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired", plus a 05:45:24Z payment-service WARN "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)"; that is staging data and I did not use it as the production root cause. In the same staging cluster the checkout workload looked healthy in the later part of the window: deployment `checkout` reported ready/available/updated = 1 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout), pod `checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n` was Running, and its application log over 05:15:33–06:15:33 contained only two info lines (order confirmation email at 05:34:34Z and "payment went through" at 05:56:08Z) when filtered for errors — counter-evidence against an ongoing staging checkout failure in that hour. All fault-injection flags in ConfigMap `flagd-config` (otel-demo), including `paymentFailure` and `paymentUnreachable`, are `defaultVariant: off`. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt), so no error-rate, latency or trace evidence exists for either cluster, and no production Kubernetes access is available; the production cause therefore remains unknown and the conclusion is inconclusive. Hypotheses below are staging-scoped only.

claims.text: Only one log index exists (`app-264-prod-logs`, 3 documents, green), and in the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:15:33Z–2026-11-21T06:15:33Z its `cluster` aggregation returned a single bucket `staging-eu-west-2` with doc_count 3 and its `environment` aggregation a single bucket `staging` with doc_count 3, so no production-eu-west-2 document was returned by this query.

The three log documents returned are, by their own fields, `cluster=staging-eu-west-2`, `environment=staging`, `region=eu-west-2`: `ERROR` service `checkout-service` at 2026-11-21T04:15:24Z message "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"; `ERROR` service `checkout-service` at 2026-11-21T05:15:24Z message "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"; `WARN` service `payment-service` at 2026-11-21T05:45:24Z message "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)".

In the accessible Kubernetes cluster (views return source `otel-demo`; no cluster label is exposed in the object fields) the namespace `otel-demo` holds deployment `checkout` with readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 and image `ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout`, alongside 20 other deployments all at 1/1/1.

Pod `checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n` (otel-demo) is Running with restartCount 1, startTime 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z and lastState terminated reason `Unknown`; its container log over 2026-11-21T05:15:33Z–06:15:33Z yielded 312 lines read, 307 removed by the error filter, and only two matching lines, both `severity: info`: "order confirmation email sent to \"bill@example.com\"" at 05:34:34.5Z and "payment went through (transaction_id: 69ca7d5c-89be-489b-a942-9aab9917ce42)" at 05:56:08.0Z.

ConfigMap `flagd-config` in namespace `otel-demo` defines the fault-flag set `productCatalogFailure`, `recommendationCacheFailure`, `adManualGc`, `adHighCpu`, `adFailure`, `kafkaQueueProblems`, `cartFailure`, `paymentFailure`, `paymentUnreachable`, `loadGeneratorFloodHomepage`, `imageSlowLoad`; every one has `defaultVariant: "off"` (e.g. paymentFailure variants on 1 / off 0, paymentUnreachable on true / off false), so no fault flag is switched on in this configuration.

All 16 Kubernetes events in the authorized window group as: Deployment/app-102 ScalingReplicaSet x2, Endpoints/(null namespace) FailedToCreateEndpoint x1, Pod/app-102 Created x3, Pulled x3, Scheduled x2, Started x3, ReplicaSet/app-102 SuccessfulCreate x2 — i.e. only app-102 rollout and one Endpoints failure event; no checkout-related event was returned.

The checkout pod's own application log in the last hour of the window (05:15:33Z–06:15:33Z) shows a successful charge ("payment went through", 05:56:08Z) and an order confirmation email (05:34:34Z) with no error-level line matched, so the staging `POST /api/checkout returned 500` line at 05:15:24Z does not describe a checkout that was still failing throughout that hour; the filter removed 307 of 312 lines, so error lines outside the matched pattern cannot be excluded.

Rejected: that the checkout-service 500 log line explains the production-eu-west-2 checkout 500s. The document carrying it states `cluster: staging-eu-west-2` and `environment: staging`, and the index's only cluster bucket over the whole window is `staging-eu-west-2`, so this line is staging-labelled evidence and cannot be attributed to production-eu-west-2.

Staging-only, unverified: in staging-eu-west-2 the checkout 500 at 2026-11-21T05:15:24Z was caused by an expired Stripe test credential used by the integration-test fixture (message literally says "integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"), consistent with payment-service reporting stripe-mock as the staging provider at 05:45:24Z. This says nothing about production-eu-west-2, whose payments configuration I could not inspect.

Staging-only, unverified: the earlier staging ERROR at 04:15:24Z ("deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress") may be temporally related to the 05:15:24Z checkout 500 and the 1 restart seen on otel-demo pods (all started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z), but no evidence ties the rollback, the restart or the 500 to one another, and the returned deployment images are all ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-*, so a promoted v2.3.4 image is not visible.

Establish whether `app-264-prod-logs` is supposed to receive production-eu-west-2 documents: its name suggests production but all 3 documents it holds are staging-labelled, so the log-shipping route for production should be verified before trusting its contents for this incident.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger respond again, query checkout's own error and latency signals (for example span-metric call counts by service and status for `checkout`, and client duration metrics for its payment dependency) scoped to production-eu-west-2, since neither backend answered during this investigation.

gaps: No production-eu-west-2 evidence exists in any source I could read: the single log index `app-264-prod-logs` returns only `cluster=staging-eu-west-2`, `environment=staging` documents (3 total), and my Kubernetes access reads only the staging cluster, which contains namespaces app-102, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo.

Prometheus was unavailable for every attempt (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_series, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate or latency series exist for checkout in either cluster, and no comparable latency baseline was obtained.

Jaeger was unavailable for every attempt (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there is no trace evidence of checkout spans, errors, or which dependency checkout was calling.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so whether a deployment or configuration change preceded the production 500s could not be checked.
It is unknown whether the three staging documents reflect the production incident mislabelled, a misrouted log pipeline, or an unrelated staging event; the index name and its contents disagree.

The cause of restartCount 1 on otel-demo pods (checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment), all started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z with lastState terminated reason `Unknown`, was not determined and is not established as impact.

The staging alert/incident start time could not be pinned: no metric or trace signal was readable, so the only timestamps available are writer-supplied log timestamps (04:15:24Z, 05:15:24Z, 05:45:24Z on 2026-11-21).
No log or object evidence covers production-eu-west-2 payment credentials; the stripe-test-key statement cannot be verified for production.

Query results returned no rejection for the exact name `checkout-service` in logs, but Kubernetes names the workload `checkout`; the two were not confirmed to be the same deployment, and no per-service trace or metric naming could be compared because those sources were unavailable.
next_steps: Verify log collection for production-eu-west-2 (agent/route/index target) and confirm whether `app-264-prod-logs` is a misnamed staging sink.
Re-run Prometheus and Jaeger queries for service `checkout` (and its payment dependency) scoped to production-eu-west-2 once those backends respond, comparing against a pre-incident baseline.

Check the production payment provider configuration (Stripe key validity/mock setting) and whether checkout's 500s coincide with a deploy or config change, using a change-history source that is not available here.

If staging-eu-west-2 is also in scope, re-check the 04:15:24Z deploy-v2.3.4 rollback and the expired integration-test stripe key with the staging on-call, since those are the only error lines found anywhere.

POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

notes: 3 lines outside the query window were dropped (0 before its start, 3 after its end).

No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
